examples.solution_text:
Write in index form.
$\begin{align*}x^{-2}&=\dfrac{1}{25}\\\dfrac{1}{x^{2}}&=\dfrac{1}{25}\\x^{2}&=25\\x&=5\end{align*}$
The base must be positive and unequal to $1$, so $-5$ is excluded.

Write both sides as powers of $2$.
$\begin{align*}(2^{4})^{x}&=2^{3}\\2^{4x}&=2^{3}\\4x&=3\\x&=\dfrac{3}{4}\end{align*}$

Take logarithms of both sides and use the power law.
$\begin{align*}\log_{10}(2^{x})&=\log_{10}5\\x\log_{10}2&=\log_{10}5\\x&=\dfrac{\log_{10}5}{\log_{10}2}\\x&\approx2.322\end{align*}$

Divide by $4$ to isolate the power, then take logarithms.
$\begin{align*}3^{x}&=20\\\log_{10}(3^{x})&=\log_{10}20\\x\log_{10}3&=\log_{10}20\\x&=\dfrac{\log_{10}20}{\log_{10}3}\\x&\approx2.727\end{align*}$

Divide by $5$, then write both sides with the same base.
$\begin{align*}4^{x}&=64\\4^{x}&=4^{3}\\x&=3\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: An investment of $\$12\,000$ grows at $10\%$ p.a. Its value after $n$ years is $FV=12\,000(1.10)^{n}$. Find the time required to reach $\$24\,000$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Substitute the target value, isolate the power, then take logarithms.
$\begin{align*}24\,000&=12\,000(1.10)^{n}\\2&=(1.10)^{n}\\\log_{10}2&=\log_{10}((1.10)^{n})\\\log_{10}2&=n\log_{10}(1.10)\\n&=\dfrac{\log_{10}2}{\log_{10}(1.10)}\\n&\approx7.27\end{align*}$
The investment reaches the target after approximately $7.27$ years.

coverage.summary: Authored eight worked examples covering seven distinct assessed methods, including both logarithmic and exact common-base routes after coefficient isolation. All use changed values, separate editable prompts and solutions, single-dollar mathematics and aligned independent equations. Solution prose inherits the supplied renderer's blue styling. No diagrams or continuation gutters are needed. Retained assessments were classified only; their mathematics was neither changed nor re-audited. Independent example review and actual visual capture remain subsequent stages.

examples.derivation: Index form gives x=4^(-3)=1/64, matching Book 1's negative-index logarithmic equations.
x^(-2)=1/25 gives x²=25. The positive-base restriction selects x=5 and excludes -5; 5 is also unequal to 1.
Taking base-10 logarithms gives x=log10(5)/log10(2)=2.321928…, hence 2.322 to three decimal places.
Dividing by 4 gives 3^x=20. Thus x=log10(20)/log10(3)=2.726833…, hence 2.727.
Dividing by 5 gives 4^x=64=4³, so x=3. This combines the supplied isolation scaffold and common-base method.
Substituting 24000 and dividing by 12000 gives 1.10^n=2. Therefore n=log10(2)/log10(1.10)=7.272540…, or approximately 7.27 years under the supplied model.
Taking logarithms gives (2x+1)log10(2)=1. Hence x=(1/log10(2)-1)/2=1.160964…, or 1.161.
